description: QGIS is a free and open-source geographic information system for Windows, macOS and Linux, covering map making, editing, analysis and sharing. Its cartography tools include a layout designer for large-format print maps, atlases and reports; editing tools digitise and construct points, lines, polygons and meshes with CAD-like tools and custom forms; and its processing toolbox provides a set of analysis tools that can be chained visually into reproducible workflows and extended with third-party tools. It reads and writes many data sources and formats, uses and publishes standards-based web services, and can be extended to cloud and mobile. Development follows a community model with an annual international conference and sustaining members. Coverage: generic. Access: free download; the source repository has release tags up to final-4_2_3. Licence: GNU GPL version 2 or later, owned by its contributors. Caveats: analysis quality depends on the plugins and data used, and plugins vary in maintenance. Simulation uses: preparing building, public space and hazard layers, exposure overlays and network inputs for infrastructure models, and hosting urban climate tools as plugins. Related records: the 3D City Database, OpenStreetMap and the momepy and cityseer urban form tools.
